prose:
Charles O'Neill describes a weekend of AI-assisted mathematics, reporting incremental improvements on selected number-theory problems while acknowledging limited subject expertise and incomplete understanding of the resulting work. He describes tools being strong at optimizing a chosen approach but weaker at recognizing its fundamental ceiling.

The essay explicitly says the selected problems were not resolved and describes some open-model reruns as assisted by hints. It is a first-person workflow account, not independent verification of the linked proofs, priority claims or a controlled comparison with mathematicians. Its analogy to gambling describes the author's experience rather than a diagnosis applicable to others. No proof checker or research code was run here.
highlights: Author describes increments rather than complete resolutions
Approach limits matter alongside parameter optimization
Linked mathematical claims were not independently verified
Personal intensity account is not a clinical conclusion
